title: Flat base change for coherent cohomology
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a scheme proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $k\to k'$ be a flat map of commutative rings with $k'$ a $k$-algebra. Write $X_{k'}:=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ and let $\mathcal F_{k'}$ denote the pullback of a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent, def-pc-base-change]. Then for all $i\geq0$

$$
H^i(X_{k'},\mathcal F_{k'})\cong H^i(X,\mathcal F)\otimes_k k'.
$$

In particular, if $k$ and $k'$ are algebraically closed fields with $k\subseteq k'$ [def-pc-field-extension] and $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, then

$$
\dim_{k'}H^i(X_{k'},\mathcal O_{X_{k'}})=\dim_kH^i(X,\mathcal O_X).
$$

proof.text: The structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper, hence separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and has a finite affine open cover $\mathfrak U=\{U_1,\ldots,U_r\}$ whose finite intersections are affine (a separated scheme over the affine $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has affine intersections of affine opens [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection]). Base change along $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ gives the affine cover $\mathfrak U_{k'}$ of $X_{k'}$, with $(U_J)_{k'}$ affine for every intersection. Applying [lem-pc-cech-computes] to $\mathfrak U$ and $\mathfrak U_{k'}$ identifies both cohomology groups with the corresponding Cech cohomology groups.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.5.2 (Tag 02KH), setup and affine-cover reduction

proof.text: For each multi-index $J$, write $U_J=\operatorname{Spec}A_J$ and $\mathcal F|_{U_J}=\widetilde M_J$. Then $(U_J)_{k'}=\operatorname{Spec}(A_J\otimes_k k')$ and the pullback module is $\widetilde{M_J\otimes_k k'}$, so the affine-section formula for pullbacks of quasi-coherent modules [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections], applied to $V=U_J$ and $U=(U_J)_{k'}$, gives $\Gamma((U_J)_{k'},\mathcal F_{k'})\cong\Gamma(U_J,\mathcal F)\otimes_{A_J}(A_J\otimes_k k')\cong\Gamma(U_J,\mathcal F)\otimes_k k'$. These identifications commute with all restriction maps, hence identify the Cech complex for $\mathfrak U_{k'}$ with the tensor product of the Cech complex for $\mathfrak U$ by $k'$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.5.2 (Tag 02KH), affine section calculation

proof.text: The map $k\to k'$ is flat, so tensoring with $k'$ is exact. Exactness preserves the kernels and images in the Cech complex, and therefore $H^i(C^\bullet\otimes_k k')\cong H^i(C^\bullet)\otimes_k k'$ for every $i$. Combining this with Step 1 and the Cech-complex identification of Step 2 gives the asserted isomorphism $H^i(X_{k'},\mathcal F_{k'})\cong H^i(X,\mathcal F)\otimes_k k'$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.5.2 (Tag 02KH), exactness of flat tensor product

proof.text: For algebraically closed field extensions $k\subseteq k'$, the map $k\to k'$ is flat because $k'$ is a vector space over the field $k$, so the first part applies to $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$. A $k$-basis of $H^i(X,\mathcal O_X)$ remains a $k'$-basis after tensoring, which gives $\dim_{k'}H^i(X_{k'},\mathcal O_{X_{k'}})=\dim_kH^i(X,\mathcal O_X)$.
